system_map.overview: Continuous Architecture System (CAS) orchestrates agentic governance and software delivery through modular agent skills, automated verifiers, and a centralised FlowRunner that evaluates architectural compliance, cost, and health telemetry.

agents.name: Verifier Subagent
agents.role: Performs independent verification and validation against architectural compliance rules and pull request requirements.

agents.name: Agentic Merger
agents.role: Synthesises and synchronises architecture steering rules and configurations across agent workspaces and Claude settings.

agents.name: Flow Runner
agents.role: Central orchestration engine executing multi-step CAS continuous architecture flows and action transitions.

orchestration.description: FlowRunner and GovernanceActionEngine coordinate sequential transitions, invoking specialized agent skills, verifier subagents, and compliance evaluations.

patterns.name: Multi-Adapter Agent Telemetry Normalization

tool_protocols.notes: Adapts heterogeneous tool telemetry outputs into OpenTelemetry-compatible structures.

optimisation_targets.notes: Calculates USD cost estimates and token metrics across diverse coding agents.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Enforces a common telemetry schema rather than relying on disparate runtime logs.

patterns.summary: Normalizes disparate agent runtime traces from multiple coding assistants into standard telemetry spans for unified health and cost tracking.
patterns.intent: Decouple agent execution telemetry from vendor-specific tool log formats to compute consistent governance health and financial metrics.
patterns.context: Used in the CAS dashboard and compliance system to track Claude Code, Antigravity, and other coding assistants.
forces: Multiple coding agent interfaces output diverse log schemas and timing formats.
Architecture governance requires uniform cost, token, and duration comparisons.
patterns.solution: Define concrete adapters for each agent type extending a common parsing protocol that emits AgentTelemetrySpan records and estimates USD costs.
implementation_signals: Distinct adapter classes for each provider (ClaudeCodeTelemetryAdapter, AntigravityTelemetryAdapter, CodingAgentTelemetryAdapter)
Unified calculation function estimate_agent_cost_usd
Normalization of ISO timestamps to epoch timestamps

evidence.note: Defines typed telemetry records and provider adapters to standardize span ingestion.

benefits: Single point of calculation for token spending and multi-agent resource usage.
Easy integration of new AI coding tools by adding an adapter.
costs: Adapter maintenance required whenever vendor log formats evolve.
Heuristic model provider inference when provider headers are missing.
failure_modes: Unparseable timestamp formats lead to omitted spans or incorrect epoch assignment.
Cost miscalculation when novel LLM model strings are unmapped.

patterns.reuse_notes: Can be applied to any developer tooling pipeline monitoring multiple agentic coding CLIs.

patterns.name: Agentic Governance Merger and Projection

tool_protocols.notes: Direct file manipulation and AST/markdown block splicing.

optimisation_targets.notes: Guarantees architectural steering rules are injected into agent instruction profiles without clobbering user customizations.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Injects immutable boundaries into agent runtime configs while retaining user developer settings.

patterns.summary: Injects and synchronises global architectural governance rules directly into agent instruction manifests and workspace settings.
patterns.intent: Ensure AI agents operating within a repository receive architectural boundaries without manual human prompt editing.
patterns.context: Project initialization and governance sync where global architecture rules must guide repository-level agents.
forces: Central architecture teams must enforce compliance constraints across repos.
patterns.solution: Use dedicated merger routines to project governance blocks into settings and AGENTS/CLAUDE instructions, preserving existing local configurations.
implementation_signals: Idempotent block insertion routines (merge_cas_governance_block, merge_claude_settings)
Dedicated AgenticMerger class in governance subsystem

evidence.note: Performs rule and knowledge merge operations.
Injects governance markers into local configuration stores during workspace setup.

benefits: Consistent architecture rules enforced across all agent instances.
costs: Requires strict delimiter parsing to prevent corruption of user settings.
Merge conflicts if agent configuration files deviate significantly.
failure_modes: Corrupted JSON/YAML if delimiter boundaries are partially modified by human edits.

patterns.reuse_notes: Adopt whenever enterprise or team-wide agent instructions need automated synchronization across repositories.

patterns.name: Independent Verifier Subagent Gate

tool_protocols.notes: Verifier executes static validation and audit checks.

optimisation_targets.notes: Prevents unchecked self-approval by separating the task executor from the task verifier.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Verifier operates autonomously to veto or approve proposed changes before merging.

patterns.summary: Separates work execution from compliance validation by assigning a dedicated verifier subagent with strict evaluation instructions.
patterns.intent: Prevent generative hallucination and self-serving bias by requiring a secondary verification agent to audit actions.
patterns.context: CI/CD and pull request evaluation pipelines validating architecture changes and feature implementations.
forces: Primary agents tend to rationalize their own generated code and rule compliance.
Manual human review of repetitive architectural checks creates a developer bottleneck.
patterns.solution: Define an isolated verifier subagent persona equipped with explicit acceptance criteria, strict veto power, and no authority to write feature code.
implementation_signals: Dedicated markdown agent definition files in .agents/subagents/ and .claude/agents/
Specific instructions directing the verifier to validate compliance rules without implementing changes

evidence.note: Defines verifier role, responsibility, and gating criteria for pull requests.
Claude-specific mirror of the verifier subagent.

benefits: Reduces automated regression risk and hallucinated rule adherence.
Clear audit trail for compliance verification.
costs: Additional LLM roundtrips and increased verification latency.
Potential false rejections if verifier criteria are overly rigid.
failure_modes: Verifier agent deadlocks pipeline by rejecting changes without actionable diagnostic feedback.

patterns.reuse_notes: Use as a gatekeeper in any multi-agent delivery system where task generation and verification must be decoupled.

patterns.name: State-Machine Transition Registry for Agent Actions

tool_protocols.notes: State transitions driven by domain models and action payloads.

optimisation_targets.notes: Guarantees governance state transitions conform to formal lifecycle invariants.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Prevents arbitrary agent state changes by restricting execution to registered transitions.

patterns.summary: Constrains governance and architecture actions to valid lifecycle transitions through an explicit transition registry.
patterns.intent: Prevent invalid or corrupt state mutations by agents during governance action execution.
patterns.context: Executing governance operations such as rule promotions, risk assessments, and compliance exceptions.
forces: Autonomous agents can attempt illogical state transitions when mutating architecture metadata.
System reliability demands deterministic, auditable status changes.
patterns.solution: Encapsulate allowed source-to-target state moves inside a TransitionRegistry evaluated by GovernanceActionEngine.
implementation_signals: TransitionRegistry class tracking permissible state transitions
GovernanceActionEngine dispatching validated actions
Pydantic models GovernanceAction and ResolutionResult defining action contracts

evidence.note: Validates state transitions prior to executing governance actions.
Typed contract specifying action parameters and execution results.

benefits: Prevents illegal state transitions and corrupt lifecycle states.
Audit logs capture deterministic resolution outcomes.
costs: All new governance states require explicit transition registration.
Rigid state definitions can reject edge-case recovery flows.
failure_modes: Unregistered valid transitions throw runtime rejection errors during agent execution.

patterns.reuse_notes: Applicable to any workflow where autonomous agents update task, policy, or document lifecycle statuses.

patterns.name: Pluggable LLM Client with Deterministic Mock Fallback

tool_protocols.notes: Unified invocation wrapper over LiteLLM library with mock client test double.

optimisation_targets.notes: Enables zero-cost offline regression testing and model vendor swapping.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Shields business and governance logic from direct vendor SDK dependencies.

patterns.summary: Abstracts language model invocation behind a uniform client interface paired with a deterministic mock client for offline verification.
patterns.intent: Shield agent logic from vendor-specific LLM APIs while providing reproducible offline execution without live tokens.
patterns.context: Used across FlowRunner, compliance checks, and unit/integration test suites.
forces: Direct model SDK bindings increase lock-in and complicate CI testing.
CI pipelines cannot incur non-deterministic costs or flaky remote API failures.
patterns.solution: Wrap LiteLLM calls in a LiteLLMClient and mirror its interface with a MockLLMClient that returns controlled synthetic responses.
implementation_signals: Side-by-side LiteLLMClient and MockLLMClient implementations
Standardized prompt and completion signatures

evidence.note: Mock client providing deterministic responses for tests.

benefits: Offline and CI test execution without token expenses or credential dependencies.
Easy switching between providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, local models).
costs: Mock client responses must be maintained to reflect changing real-world prompt contracts.
Subtle live-model behavioral divergences are missed during mock runs.
failure_modes: Mock responses get out of sync with updated Pydantic parsing schemas.

patterns.reuse_notes: Essential baseline pattern for any production agent system requiring CI testability.

patterns.name: Declarative Agent Skill Packaging

tool_protocols.notes: Self-contained skill manifests and prompt guides.

optimisation_targets.notes: Allows agents to load targeted contextual skills on demand.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Modular capabilities can be plugged into different agent engines without code alterations.

patterns.summary: Packages discrete agent capabilities and domain prompts into isolated, declarative skill bundles shared across agent runtimes.
patterns.intent: Prevent monolithic system prompts by organizing capabilities into modular, individually testable skill packages.
patterns.context: Agent execution across repository tasks such as DrawIO generation, knowledge link refactoring, and rule auditing.
forces: Monolithic system prompts exceed context windows and degrade agent attention.
Different agent hosts (Claude CLI, internal CLI runner) need consistent skill definitions.
patterns.solution: Organize skills as modular directories under `.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/` with standardized task boundaries.
implementation_signals: Dedicated directories under .agents/skills/ for each capability
Mirroring into .claude/skills/ for Claude Code compatibility
Skills include cas-drawio-generator, cas-sync-archgov-reviews, cas-audit-agent-rules

evidence.note: Modular skill package for generating DrawIO architecture diagrams.
Skill package for auditing repository compliance against agent steering rules.
Skill package for syncing architectural review outcomes into repository governance.

benefits: Composable agent capabilities loaded on demand.
Cross-runtime portability between standalone CLI and Claude Code.
costs: Duplication or symlink management needed across agent directory structures.
failure_modes: Skill definitions falling out of sync between `.agents/skills` and `.claude/skills`.

patterns.reuse_notes: Ideal structure for building reusable agent capability libraries across organizations.

patterns.name: Sequential Governance Flow Runner

tool_protocols.notes: Steps invoke compliance engine, state transitions, and file generators in order.

optimisation_targets.notes: Guarantees deterministic multi-step pipeline execution of governance and validation steps.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Linear step-based pipeline prioritises predictable execution order over emergent multi-agent looping.

patterns.summary: Executes continuous architecture workflows as a deterministic sequential pipeline passing structured context across steps.
patterns.intent: Orchestrate multi-phase architecture workflows (audit, validate, generate, review) with consistent error boundaries.
patterns.context: Executing CAS CLI commands and CI/CD automated continuous architecture jobs.
forces: Uncoordinated agent actions create race conditions when mutating shared knowledge bases.
Architecture workflows have strict prerequisite dependencies (e.g., validate before publishing).
patterns.solution: Implement a FlowRunner class that manages ordered execution of discrete governance steps, passing intermediate contexts.
implementation_signals: FlowRunner class in src/cas_runner/runner.py
CLI dispatch to flow runners in src/cas_runner/cli.py
Integration with ComplianceEngine and GovernanceActionEngine

evidence.note: Coordinates execution flow across architecture steps.
Entry point invoking flow runners based on command line arguments.

benefits: Deterministic execution trace and clear step-level failure reporting.
Simple execution model that is easy to debug in CI/CD environments.
costs: Cannot dynamically adapt flow order in response to runtime discoveries without custom step logic.
failure_modes: An unhandled exception in an early step halts the entire governance cycle without checkpointing.

patterns.reuse_notes: Recommended for pipeline-oriented agent workflows where deterministic ordering is critical.

patterns.name: Architecture-as-Code Contextual Rule Binding

tool_protocols.notes: Static JSON/YAML files bound into evaluation engines.

optimisation_targets.notes: Grounds agent prompt context in version-controlled architectural constraints.

simplicity_vs_autonomy.rationale: Static declarative artifacts provide durable ground truth over LLM parametric memory.

patterns.summary: Maintains persistent architecture decisions, patterns, and rule contexts in version control to bind agent reasoning to validated invariants.
patterns.intent: Ground agent reasoning and compliance checks in explicit, versioned architectural decisions rather than implicit model assumptions.
patterns.context: cas-knowledge repository directory feeding rule contexts into ComplianceEngine and agent skills.
forces: LLMs hallucinate or drift from organization-specific architectural conventions over time.
Architecture patterns and decisions evolve dynamically across project lifecycles.
patterns.solution: Store architecture rules, patterns, decisions, and signals as structured markdown and JSON files, compiled into runtime execution profiles.
implementation_signals: cas-knowledge/ directory containing decisions/, patterns/, rules/, and signals/
Structured schemas rule-context.json and execution-profile.yaml in cas-knowledge/runtime/
ComplianceEngine and ComplianceFinding models checking code against these artifacts

evidence.note: Compiled rule context JSON providing explicit constraint definitions for agents.
Declares runtime profile binding active rules to target environments.
Evaluates project code against rule context specifications.

benefits: Auditable, git-backed architecture source of truth.
Immediate reflection of architectural updates across all agent evaluations.
costs: Requires systematic curation of markdown and JSON governance templates.
Token overhead when injecting full rule contexts into prompts.
failure_modes: Stale rule context bindings leading agents to enforce deprecated architectural patterns.

patterns.reuse_notes: Use in continuous architecture environments to bridge organizational knowledge and agent prompt spaces.

anti_patterns.name: Unmanaged Agent Setting Divergence
symptoms: Agents configured under .claude/ operating with conflicting rules compared to agents configured in .agents/
Developers overriding local configuration files and accidentally stripping governance steering sections

where_observed.note: Code specifically introduces delimiter-based merging to counter manual configuration drift across agent directories.

impact: Agents in different IDE environments execute with inconsistent constraints, causing inconsistent PR validation outcomes.
suggested_remediation: Enforce automated pre-commit and CI verification checks to ensure agent steering blocks are identical and intact across all agent manifests.

anti_patterns.name: Silent Mock Client Slippage into Runtime
symptoms: Compliance checks passing in CI due to deterministic canned mock responses without live reasoning taking place
Absence of runtime environment guards enforcing live API keys when non-dry-run actions are triggered

where_observed.note: Mock client provides hardcoded canned responses that could mask real failure modes if enabled outside test suites.

impact: False sense of governance compliance in production workflows where genuine architectural regressions go undetected.
suggested_remediation: Explicitly disallow MockLLMClient instantiation unless a dedicated environment variable (e.g. CAS_TEST_MODE=1) is present.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Unified OpenTelemetry span generation and USD cost calculations across heterogeneous coding agent logs via dedicated telemetry adapters.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Normalizing telemetry at ingest prevents downstream dashboard calculations from being coupled to individual vendor log schemas.

cross_cutting_concerns.approach: Dual-control verification where generation skills are distinct from the verifier subagent and constrained by state-machine transition rules.
cross_cutting_concerns.notes: Restricting autonomous agents from performing arbitrary status promotions directly addresses alignment and drift risks.

open_questions.question: How are concurrent agent executions coordinated if multiple developers or CI jobs run FlowRunner simultaneously?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Simultaneous updates to cas-knowledge git structures could lead to merge conflicts or lost governance updates.
open_questions.evidence_gap: FlowRunner does not explicitly show distributed locking or mutex semantics in runner.py.
open_questions.suggested_next_check: Inspect GitHub Actions workflows (cas-continuous-architecture.yml) for repository concurrency locks or git commit retry logic.
